subject: Private CP: SAML assertion mapping and SCIM provisioning for service accounts
messages:
From: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Tim Bell <tim.bell@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private CP SSO/SCIM discussion kickoff

Hi Priyom / Laura,

Thanks again for taking this. We’re starting the private control plane deployment for our EU/US clusters and need to align on identity for service accounts and admin roles. Two concrete asks to start:

1) Confirm recommended SAML attribute mapping for admin vs read-only roles (we use Azure AD and have groups: RedwoodAdmins, RedwoodViewers, InfraOps).
2) Confirm SCIM provisioning flow for machine/service accounts (create, patch, deprovision) and whether we should provision them as "bot" user objects or as service-account records via SCIM extension.

Attached: acme_sso_requirements.pdf, scim_schema.csv

High level constraints: no inbound internet connectivity to the private control plane; SAML assertions will be proxied through our SP-initiated proxy in the VPC. We also need guidance on short-lived service account credentials and rotation policies to meet our internal audit.

Can we get a proposed mapping and a short runbook for lifecycle within 3 business days? We’re aiming for a staging cutover next Wednesday (2026-12-22).

Best,
Samantha
Security & Identity, Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme_sso_requirements.pdf (PDF, 78KB)]
[Attachment: scim_schema.csv (CSV, 6KB)]

Subject: Re: Private CP SSO/SCIM discussion kickoff

Hi Samantha — thanks for the context and attachments. Quick ack: we can produce the mapping and a concise lifecycle runbook. Preliminary plan below and we’ll follow up with a technical note and example assertions: 

- SAML group->role mapping: suggest using Group Membership with attribute urn:eduPersonEntitlement or groups claim, mapping to internal role names: Redwood.Admin -> admin role, Redwood.Viewer -> viewer role, Infra.Ops -> infra role. We’ll provide exact attribute names for Azure AD (group object IDs vs group names)
- SCIM model: recommend representing service accounts as SCIM Users with a custom extension attribute "urn:redwood:serviceAccount:true" = true. This avoids adding a new resource type in the customer SCIM endpoint.
- Lifecycle: create (POST /Users), update / patch for keys and TTL (PATCH), soft-deprovision by setting active=false + retention TTL, final delete after retention.

Blocked items:
- We need the SAML response sample (encoded) or metadata to validate assertion conditions given your SP proxy.
- Clarify whether your SCIM endpoint can accept PATCH operations for hashed keys.

I’ll draft the runbook and an assertion-to-role mapping matrix this afternoon and drop a link.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-sso-onboarding-runbook]

Samantha / team — a couple of clarifying questions so our runbook is prescriptive:

1) Service account auth model: do you want short-lived API keys minted by Redwood after SCIM create (recommended), or do you prefer long-lived keys stored in your vault and pushed via SCIM attribute? We favor our short-lived approach to meet audit.
2) Namespace isolation: will each environment (staging/prod) use distinct group namespaces or will groups overlap across environments? This impacts our role resolution: prefer environment-scoped groups (e.g., RedwoodAdmins_prod).
3) Role escalation flow: if a user is in multiple groups, do you want the highest privilege to apply or explicit deny precedence? We need that policy for assertion evaluation.

Also: we’ll include an example SCIM PATCH payload and an Azure AD manifest snippet. Rishi, can you outline key rotation and HSM/KMS integration notes?

Thanks,
Laura
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@acme-corp.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private CP: SAML assertion mapping and SCIM provisioning for service accounts

Thanks — adding technical detail below (example-friendly):

1) Example SAML Assertion (Azure AD) we recommend validating:
- Subject: NameID format = urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress
- Attributes: 
  - http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/Group -> array of group display names or objectIds
  - http://schemas.microsoft.com/identity/claims/objectidentifier -> user id
  - urn:redwood:env -> staging|prod (optional)

Mapping rules (pseudo):
- if groups contains "RedwoodAdmins" OR objectId IN [list-of-admin-ids] -> role = "admin"
- else if groups contains "RedwoodViewers" -> role = "viewer"
- else if groups contains "InfraOps" -> role = "infra"

Precedence: highest privilege wins; we’ll optionally support explicit deny via attribute urn:redwood:deny=true if you need deny semantics. Please confirm.

2) SCIM provisioning for service accounts (recommended flow):
- Create: POST /Users with {userName: "svc_<app>-<env>", displayName: "svc: <app> (<env>)", active: true, urn:redwood:serviceAccount:true = true, urn:redwood:keyThumbprint = <pubkey-thumbprint>}
- Key rotation: Redwood will accept PATCH operations to replace urn:redwood:keyThumbprint; upon patch, we rotate internal ephemeral credential and mark previous as revoked. Recommend TTL on keys 24h–72h depending on risk profile.
- Deprovision: set active=false + add meta.deletedReason and a deletionScheduled timestamp; a lifecycle job runs after retention window to hard-delete.

3) Networking / proxy notes for the private control plane:
- Since you proxy SAML through an SP in the VPC, ensure the SP preserves the original AssertionConsumerService URL in RelayState so we can validate audience and recipient constraints.
- SCIM calls must originate from your SCIM proxy IPs or via mutual TLS client certs. We support mTLS and token-based bearer; recommend mTLS for on-prem SCIM endpoints.

4) Evidence for audit: we’ll produce an export of SCIM events (create/patch/delete) and assertion validation logs scoped to the integration for your SOC team. That can be retained per your retention policy.

Example SCIM PATCH snippet (JSON):
PATCH /Users/2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/scim+json

{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [{
    "op": "Replace",
    "path": "urn:redwood:keyThumbprint",
    "value": "sha256:QmFzZTY0U2FtcGxl"
  }]
}

5) HubSpot / next steps: I’ve linked the technical note to the deal (DEAL-7382) and created a short checklist for the staging cutover. Priyom — I left two items for your team to confirm (SAML sample + SCIM PATCH support).

— Rishi

Redwood Inference
